summary: RevOps: add HubSpot properties to track pricing experiment cohort + pricing plan exposure
description:
Request (RevOps/Product Ops)

We need new HubSpot properties to track (a) which pricing experiment cohort/variant a company is in and (b) which Hosted API pricing plan/package they are currently on. This is required for:
- experiment reporting and cohort QA (ensure eligibility / exposure is consistent)
- sales visibility (AEs/CSMs can see why pricing shown differs)
- contracting & discount approvals (avoid stacking discounts on experimental pricing)

Background
- Q1 pricing & packaging experiments are ongoing and the analysis plan requires reliable cohort tagging in CRM.
- Meter fixes are landing in parallel; analyses need “pre/post meter fix” segmentation and a way to annotate affected accounts.

Where properties should live
- Primary: Company object (source-of-truth for account-level cohort exposure)
- Optional: Deal object (to capture plan at time of contract/expansion)

Requested Company properties (proposed)
1) ri_pricing_experiment_id
- Type: single-line text
- Example: "2026Q1-HOSTED-PACKAGING-VAR-B"
- Notes: stable identifier; do not repurpose across experiments.

2) ri_pricing_experiment_variant
- Type: dropdown select
- Allowed values: "control", "variant_a", "variant_b", "variant_c", "holdout", "unknown"
- Default: "unknown"

3) ri_pricing_experiment_exposure_date
- Type: date
- Definition: first date the company/account was eligible + saw the variant in-product (not merely flagged in backend).

4) ri_hosted_api_pricing_plan
- Type: dropdown select
- Allowed values (initial): "Free", "Starter", "Pro", "Enterprise", "Dedicated Add-on", "Unknown"
- Notes: we can iterate values once Packaging Variants v3 is finalized; for now keep coarse.

5) ri_metering_semantics_version
- Type: dropdown select
- Allowed values: "v1", "v2", "mixed/transition", "unknown"
- Definition: which metering definition set applies for reporting (to reduce confusion during meter hardening).

6) ri_pricing_experiment_notes
- Type: multi-line text
- Usage: short operational notes (e.g., "excluded from analysis due to custom contract", "manual override approved by Finance").

Data source + sync expectations
- Preferred source-of-truth: warehouse export maintained by Product Ops (daily), derived from experiment cohort tagging + billing system plan metadata.
- Initial backfill needed for existing active companies impacted since 2026-01-01.
- Ongoing updates: daily (or at minimum weekly) to keep sales views accurate.

Access controls
- Editable by: RevOps Ops team only (to prevent accidental changes)
- Visible to: Sales, CS, Finance (read-only)

Timeline / urgency
- Needed by: 2026-02-21 (to support next experiment readout + sales enablement rollout)

Open questions to confirm
- Should we also add Deal-level snapshots (plan at close date) to support RevRec and prevent later edits from rewriting history?
- Should we use one property for "current plan" and another for "plan at first exposure"?

Requester: Chris Osei (Product Ops) on behalf of Evelyn Hart / Jordan Blake pricing experiment workflow.
comments:
2026-02-07 (Chris Osei)
Adding context: the current workaround is a spreadsheet + manual notes in HubSpot. It’s not scalable and has already caused 2 accounts to be mis-labeled in the readout draft.

2026-02-08 (Talia Benson)
Acknowledged. I’ll coordinate with RevOps to confirm naming conventions + who owns the warehouse-to-HubSpot sync. Proposed approach:
1) Create properties on Company (and optionally Deal)
2) Backfill via import (CSV) for last ~60 days
3) Add scheduled sync job (daily) once schema is stable

2026-02-10 (Talia Benson)
Quick question: for "ri_pricing_experiment_exposure_date" do we want first exposure timestamp (UTC) vs date? HubSpot date fields drop time. If time matters for analysis, we can store ISO timestamp in a text field and keep date separately.

2026-02-10 (Chris Osei)
Date is fine for CRM workflows. For analysis we’ll use the warehouse timestamp anyway.

2026-02-12 (Talia Benson)
RevOps confirmed we should avoid frequent dropdown value changes. Suggest we start with conservative dropdown values and store the detailed plan code in text.
Proposed add’l property:
- ri_hosted_api_plan_code (single-line text) e.g., "hosted_pro_v3" / "hosted_starter_expB"

2026-02-13 (Chris Osei)
+1. Plan code will be useful for the cohort definitions doc and to reconcile with billing exports.

2026-02-18 (Talia Benson)
Implementation update:
- Properties created in HubSpot sandbox for review
- Pending approval on final names (prefix "ri_" vs "redwood_")
- Backfill file ready once names locked

2026-02-20 (Talia Benson)
Moved to In Progress. Next steps:
- Create in production
- Run backfill import for impacted companies
- Add to Sales "Account Overview" view + filter presets for experiment tracking
- Document in RevOps runbook (who can edit, how to request changes)
acceptance_criteria:
1) Company properties exist in HubSpot prod with agreed names and types.
2) Properties are visible to Sales/CS/Finance and restricted to RevOps for edits.
3) Backfill completed for active companies with cohort exposure since 2026-01-01.
4) At least one saved view/filter is available to Sales: "Pricing Experiment Cohorts" (filter by experiment_id/variant/plan).
5) A documented process exists for (a) adding new variants/experiments and (b) handling manual overrides/exclusions.
risk_notes:
Risks:
- Dropdown values changing mid-experiment can break reporting and filters.
- If we overwrite cohort/plan history, CRM will not reflect what the customer saw at the time of negotiation.
- Metering changes overlapping experiment windows can cause confusion; "ri_metering_semantics_version" should be treated as reporting annotation only.
Mitigations:
- Store detailed plan code in text; keep dropdown coarse.
- Consider a Deal-level snapshot property set at deal stage transition (e.g., at Closed Won) to preserve history.
